overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law in most respects: vague notice topics, missing litigation disclosure, no verbal topic statement, improper private discussion, and denial of the subject's open-session request, but upheld the litigation discussion as Purpose 3 and ordered release of improperly withheld minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the meeting notice's executive session topics were too vague to tell the public what would be discussed.
allegations.key_passage: were vague and failed to give a reasonable member of the public an idea as to what the Board would be discussing.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the notice failed to disclose that the executive session would include discussion of pending litigation.
allegations.key_passage: the Board should still have indicated on the meeting notice that it would be discussing a litigation matter during the executive session.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the chair did not verbally identify the executive session topics before the board convened in private.
allegations.key_passage: Such a description of the topics to be discussed is required prior to convening in executive session.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged executive session discussions did not fit any statutory purpose, including budget and board-authority topics.
allegations.key_passage: Discussions of the Water Department budget and the Board's authority relative to the Board of Selectmen do not fit within any of the ten statutory purposes for executive session.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the executive session discussion of pending litigation against the board lacked a proper purpose.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the discussion of pending litigation against the Board was appropriate for discussion during an executive session.

allegations.summary: Complainant, the subject of an executive session discussion, alleged the board wrongly denied her request to have the discussion held in open session.
allegations.key_passage: The Board therefore violated the Open Meeting Law by denying Ms. Wiser's request to hold the portion of the discussion that involved her in open session.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the chair took actions outside his authority as chair; the AG considered this not an Open Meeting Law issue.
allegations.key_passage: This allegation, even if true, would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law. We therefore decline to review it.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.

Release to the public of the executive session minutes portions concerning the Water Department budget and the Board's authority relative to the Board of Selectmen, within ten days of receipt of the letter.
remedy_passage: We order the Board's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
